# Content and UX Language

## Voice

- Precise
- Calm
- Non-promotional
- Evidence-aware
- Neutral about Proceed and No-Go
- Explicit about consequences

## Information origins

Use consistent language for:

- User-authored
- Imported
- Inherited
- Computed
- AI-suggested
- Validated
- Superseded

## Messages

A useful system message:

1. names the object or action;
2. states what happened;
3. says whether user work was preserved;
4. explains why the condition matters;
5. provides one concrete next action.

Avoid:

- “Something went wrong.”
- “No data.”
- “Are you sure?”
- “AI recommendation” without qualification.
- vague success messages.

## AI language

Prefer:

> Suggested from current evidence. Not yet accepted by a consultant.

Avoid language that transfers accountability to the model.

## Provenance language

Example:

> Inherited from Station 03 · authored by A. Imboden · 18 March

## No-Go language

Describe closure as an explicit decision. State what remains readable and how the case can be reopened.
